s: Masterless wide-column store built for linear write scaling and multi-datacenter survival.
w: Consistent hashing rings distribute partition keys; ANY quorum levels tune consistency per query (ONE/QUORUM/ALL). Writes go to commitlog + memtables flushed to SSTables, compacted in background. Every node is identical - no primary to fall over. Replication factors span DCs natively; tunable consistency lets you pick AP-leaning or CP-leaning per operation.
use: Write-heavy ingest: telemetry, messages, clickstreams at huge volume
Always-available writes across regions (shopping carts, activity feeds)
Time-bucketed histories (chat logs, device timelines) queried by key
Linear horizontal growth without manual sharding layers
avoid: Ad-hoc joins/aggregations - model tables per query instead
Small datasets where operational overhead isn't justified

props.partition_key: Design FIRST around queries; random token avoids hotspots

pat.d: Append-only event streams partitioned by entity id.

pits: Bad partition design = unfixable hotspots later - model queries first, literally
Compaction stalls spike latencies - tune compaction strategy per workload
GC pauses at big heaps - keep heaps ≤14GB, prefer many medium nodes
tips: CAP nuance: Cassandra is 'effectively AP with tunable C' - say it precisely
Quote Discord/Apple numbers sparingly but credibly when asked about proof at scale
